title: What Is the Minimum Wage in Australia? Hourly, Annual, Fortnightly and Tax Explained
description: Find out what is the minimum wage in Australia for 2026-27. Learn how to convert $26.44 per hour to annual, fortnightly pay, plus tax and super on top.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, the annual gross pay is approximately $52,277, with super and tax estimated on top.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage per hour in Australia from 1 July 2026?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive at least $33.05 per hour including 25% loading.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week (typically 38) then by 52 weeks. For the minimum wage, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,277.44 gross per year.

faqs.q: Is superannuation paid on top of the minimum wage?
faqs.a: Yes, the super guarantee of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings. For minimum wage, that adds about $6,273 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the National Minimum Wage

If you have ever asked yourself **what is the minimum wage** in Australia, the answer from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult employee working 38 hours per week. This figure is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. For casual workers, the minimum wage includes a 25% loading, bringing the casual rate to $33.05 per hour. The weekly minimum for a 38-hour week is $1,004.90 before tax and super.

It is important to distinguish the National Minimum Wage from award rates. Awards set higher minimums for specific industries and roles. For example, a hospitality award may have a higher base rate than the national minimum. The figures here are the legal floor, not a median or average for any particular job. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, but that is an average across all occupations, not a minimum or a median for your role.

## Converting Hourly to Annual: The Formula

To estimate your annual gross pay from an hourly rate, use the standard formula:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a standard full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week as per the Fair Work Act. For the National Minimum Wage:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,277.44 per year

If you are a casual worker on the minimum wage including loading:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,302.80 per year

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For the minimum wage:

Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (rounded)
Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44

Knowing your fortnightly gross helps with budgeting and comparing to salary offers. You can use [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly estimates instantly.

## Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave entitlements. This loading is applied to the minimum wage, so the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When using a calculator, always enter your base hourly rate *before* casual loading. A checkbox then adds the 25% on top. Never enter a rate that already includes loading, as that would double-count.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a minimum-wage employee earning $52,277.44, super adds about $6,273.29 per year. This is paid by your employer into your super fund and is not deducted from your take-home pay. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax on Your Minimum Wage Earnings

For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (generally). For a minimum-wage earner with gross annual pay of $52,277.44, the estimated tax (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here) would be approximately:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 (to $45,000): $26,800 × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $7,277.44 (to $52,277.44): $7,277.44 × 30% = $2,183.23
- Total tax: $6,203.23
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,277.44): $1,045.55
- Total tax and Medicare: $7,248.78

Take-home pay after tax and Medicare: $52,277.44 – $7,248.78 = $45,028.66 per year, or about $866 per week. This is an estimate only. Your actual tax may vary if you have HELP debt, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) topic for more detail.

## Award Rates vs Minimum Wage

Many employees are covered by an award that sets a higher minimum wage than the National Minimum Wage. For example, the General Retail Industry Award has different pay rates for different classifications. The National Minimum Wage is the absolute floor; if your award rate is higher, your employer must pay that higher rate. Casual loading also applies on top of award rates unless the award already includes a loaded rate. Check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use our [pay guides](/blog) to find the correct rate for your job.

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [reference tables](/data) provide quick lookups for common pay points, but the most accurate way to see your own figures is to use [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate (before casual loading), select your hours per week (default 38), and the calculator will show your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. A checkbox adds 25% casual loading if applicable. Remember, super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings and is paid on top, not deducted from your pay. The calculator follows the formula: hourly × hours per week × 52.

If you are comparing a salary offer, convert the annual salary to an hourly rate by dividing by (hours per week × 52). For a 38-hour week, that is dividing by 1,976. Then compare with the minimum wage or your award rate. For more on this, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).

### A Note on Averages and Medians

This article focuses on the minimum wage. The Australian Bureau of Statistics publishes average weekly earnings, but those are averages across all full-time adults, not medians for a specific job. For example, the May 2026 average full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week, but that does not represent the typical pay for any single occupation. If you need a job-specific figure, consult your award or industry agreement. Our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) topic may help, but we do not invent medians.

## Summary

- National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026: $26.44 per hour, $1,004.90 per week (38 hours)
- Casual rate including 25% loading: $33.05 per hour
- Annual gross for minimum wage: $52,277.44
- Super guarantee of 12% paid on top
- Tax and Medicare estimated at about $7,249 per year for a full-time minimum wage earner
- Always check your award for higher rates

Understanding **what is the minimum wage** is the first step to evaluating any pay offer. Use our tools to convert your hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and remember that super and casual loading are separate additions.
